seoTitle: Forward a Squarespace-Hosted Domain to Another Site
metaDescription: Set up domain forwarding directly in Squarespace's dashboard, with redirect type, SSL, and path forwarding options explained.
intro: Squarespace lets you forward a domain to another website without touching DNS or transferring the domain itself. This guide covers the built-in Forwarding feature, including choosing a redirect type and deciding whether to preserve URL paths.

steps.heading: Open the Forwarding section
steps.body: Log in to Squarespace, select the site, then go to Website in the left sidebar and scroll to Forwarding. Click Add Rule to start.

steps.heading: Set the subdomain and destination
steps.body: Enter @ to forward your root domain or www for that subdomain, then enter the full destination URL you want traffic sent to.

steps.heading: Choose a redirect type
steps.body: Under Advanced Settings, pick Permanent Redirect (301) if the original domain is retired, or Temporary Redirect (302) if it will be used again later.

steps.heading: Enable SSL
steps.body: Turn SSL on so the redirect works for both HTTP and HTTPS traffic, keeping in mind it can take up to 48 hours to fully propagate.

steps.heading: Set path forwarding and save
steps.body: Choose Remove Paths to send every page to the new site's homepage, or Maintain Paths to preserve the original URL structure, then click Save.

faq.question: Do I need to change my DNS records to forward a Squarespace domain?
faq.answer: No, Squarespace's Forwarding feature handles this without requiring manual DNS or .htaccess changes.

faq.question: What's the difference between a 301 and 302 redirect?
faq.answer: A 301 is permanent and tells search engines the move is final, while a 302 is temporary and signals the original domain may return.

faq.question: How long does it take for forwarding to fully work?
faq.answer: It can take up to 48 hours for the redirect, especially with SSL enabled, to propagate fully.

faq.question: Should I choose Remove Paths or Maintain Paths?
faq.answer: Choose Remove Paths if you want all traffic sent to the new site's homepage, or Maintain Paths if you want each URL to map to the same path on the destination site.
